correctness.rationale: The polynomial moment identities were reconstructed by exact disk monomial integration and checked symbolically. The phase term is strictly maximized by alignment at nonzero amplitudes; maximizing over linear squared energy has an exact unique stationary maximum for every quadratic-to-constant ratio; the remaining derivative has a single positive quartic root by Descartes and continuity; zero-constant boundary and each two-degree subspace are optimized separately. The entire equality family follows from strict steps. The companion checker passed exact identities and 100 independent high-order quadrature comparisons. Numeric trials are not treated as the global proof.

originality.rationale: The full real harmonic degree-at-most-two disk moment optimization, its single quartic-root sharp constant and complete equality classification, and the strict exact two-degree barrier were compared against accessible primary papers on harmonic Hardy inequalities, spherical Nikolskii inequalities, analytic Bergman hypercontractivity, and hyperbolic harmonic Bergman projection. A close published claim concerns only a homogeneous degree-two spherical-harmonic space. The disk probability measure is the marginal of S^3, but the present non-lacunary constant + degree-one + degree-two space is not covered by a homogeneous or lacunary theorem. Searches did not yield an equivalent numerical constant or full theorem; this is a best-knowledge assessment, not proof of historical uniqueness.
residual_risks: Equivalent sharp finite-band norm under Zernike polynomials or a spherical-marginal identity may exist in unindexed literature.
Full-text inspection concentrated on the main theorems, hypotheses and relevant proof material; not every line of all long related sources was rederived.
No independent priority certification or external mathematical peer review.

value.rationale: The entire natural five-dimensional space of real harmonic disk polynomials of degree at most two is classified in one sharp inequality. Exact strict gap K_*-297/86 means a nontrivial interference of constant, linear and quadratic harmonic degrees is essential. This resolves a motivated finite-band harmonic Bergman norm question, provides a definite comparison point for other norms/weights and does not rely on arbitrary coefficient restrictions, unknown downstream theorems or merely numerical novelty.
